rawFindings.title: `is.current('/')` no longer matches the homepage path
rawFindings.explanation: The helper now defaults `path` to an empty string and compares `this.path` directly in strict mode. For the homepage, `this.path` is typically `index.html`, so `is.current.call({path: 'index.html'}, '/')` now returns false instead of true. This breaks the common template check for the current homepage.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore normalization of the current path and treat `'/'` as `/index.html` (or equivalent) before comparing.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Calling `is.current` from the homepage context with `path='/'` returns false even though the homepage is current.

rawFindings.title: Non-strict matching no longer recognizes directory paths
rawFindings.explanation: The non-strict branch now does a raw prefix comparison against `this.path` without normalizing either operand. As a result, `is.current.call({path: 'tags/index.html'}, 'tags')` returns false, whereas the previous implementation matched directory URLs by prepending a leading slash and handling `/index.html` suffixes.
rawFindings.suggestion: Normalize both `this.path` and `path` before prefix comparison, preserving support for directory-style inputs and `/index.html` aliases.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: On a page whose path is `tags/index.html`, `is.current('tags')` now returns false instead of true.
